sentences.text: This reference made by the respondent No.1/SLAO, KIADB (Metro Rail Project), Bengaluru under Sections 30 and 31(2) of L.A. Act, 1894 (L.A. Act, L.A.C. No. 133/2016 1894 for short), for apportionment of compensation amount.

.2. As per the records, the respondent No.1 has acquired the property measuring 6 sq. meters in Sy.No.33/2 of Pattanagere village for the purpose of BMRCL under Preliminary Notification dated 29.12.2014 and Final Notification dated 16/17.10.2015.
The award passed on 11.05.2016, fixing compensation of Rs.8,55,364/- in this case.

As title documents were not produced, the L.A.O. has referred the matter to this Court and has deposited a sum of Rs.6,84,291/- after deducting 20%
Income tax.
The said amount has been kept in F.D. in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Extension counter, Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of the reference, this court issued notice to both parties.
In pursuance of notice, the claimants 1, 2 and 4 had entered appearance and the claimant No.2 and 4 filed claim statements.
The L.A.C. No. 133/2016 claimant No. 3 though served with the notice not chosen to appear before the Court to resist the case and hence, he has been placed exparte.

.4 . The claimant No.2 Lakshmi K filed claim statement stating that she is the absolute owner of composite land bearing Sy. No. 33/2 (old Sy. No.33) along with other survey numbers measuring to an extent of 1 acre 27 guntas (83743.90 Sq. feet), situated at Pattanagere village, Kengeri Hobli,
Bangaluru South Taluka.

She has further stated that originally the said land belongs to one Smt.

2 Geetha and others, who in turn, have sold the same to Smt. Gopamma - claimant No.1, Smt.
Lakshmi - claimant No.2 and G.C. Chandrashekar - claimant No. 3 through registered sale deed and thereafter their names have been mutated in the revenue records.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the claimants 1 to 3 have partitioned the said land along with other lands.

As per the said partition, the composite land bearing Sy.
L.A.C. No. 133/2016 No. 33/2 along with other survey numbers measuring to an extent of 1 acre 27 guntas has fallen to the share of claimant No.2.
Consequent to the said partition deed dated 22.03.1991 the claimant No. 2 has become owner of the said property.
In the meantime, the respondent No. 1 KIADB has acquired the said property for the purpose of Metro Rail Project.

She has further stated that out of 6 Sq. Meters acquired by the respondent, the land measuring to an extent of 3 Sq. Meters is owned by claimant No. 4 and remaining 3 Sq. Meters is that of the land owned by the claimant No. 2.

As per the family partition deed dated 01.09.2017 the claimant No. 1 has no right over the property in question and the property belongs to the claimant No. 3 has not acquired under the above said notification.
Hence, the claimants 1 and 3 are the formal parties to the above said proceedings.

.5. The claimant No. 4 Gajendra has filed claim statement stating that he is the absolute owner of the L.A.C. No. 133/2016 composite land bearing Sy. No. 33/2 along with other survey numbers measuring to an extent of 2 acres 25 guntas (111128 Sq. feet), situated at Pattanagere village, Kengeri Hobli, Bangaluru South Taluka.

He has further stated that originally the said land beings to one Smt. Geetha and others, who in turn, have sold the same to Smt. Gopamma - claimant No. 1, Smt.
Lakshmi - claimant No. 2 and G.C. Chandrashekar - claimant No. 3 through registered sale deed and thereafter their names have been mutated in the revenue records.
Thereafter, the claimants 1 to 3 have partitioned the said land along with other lands.

As per the said partition, the property in question has been divided along with other properties among the claimants 1 to 3 and they have taken the possession of their respective shares and accordingly, the revenue entries made in respective names.

He has further stated that after the aforesaid partition, the claimant No.1 has executed a registered family settlement deed along with her other family members in favour of claimant No. 4 and hence he has become the absolute owner of the property measuring to an extent of 2 acres 25 guntas.

He further stated that out of 6 Sq. Meters acquired by the respondent, the land measuring to an extent of 3 Sq. Meters is owned by him and remaining 3 Sq. Meters is that of the land owned by the claimant No. 2.

As per the family partition deed dated 01.09.2017 the claimant No.1 has no right over the property in question and the property belongs to the claimant No. 3 has not acquired under the above said notification.
Hence, the claimants 1 and 3 are the formal parties to the above said proceedings.
Hence, prayed for apportionment of compensation amount.

.7. The respondent No. 1 has filed objections stating that the claimants have not filed their title deeds L.A.C. No. 133/2016 to establish their right and title and hence the above reference has been sent to the Court for apportionment of compensation.
Hence, prayed to pass the suitable orders.

sentences.text: The respondent No. 2 BMRCL has filed objections stating that the beneficiary of acquisition BMRCL sent the package compensation of Rs. 8,55,364/- to the SLAO, KIADB in respect of acquired property measuring 6 Sq. Meters determining the market value at Rs. 63,292/- per Sq. Meters through letter dated 29.01.2016.
However, khatedar or any other person interested in the aforesaid acquired property neither attended the inquiry nor submitted documents of title over the acquired property proving their ownership.
Hence, the SLAO deposited a sum of Rs. 8,55,364/- into the City Civil Court after deducting 20% income tax.

In view of the said deposit, the respondent No. 2 BMRCL who is beneficiary of L.A.C. No. 133/2016 acquisition will not be liable to pay interest on the awarded compensation amount as held in the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in 1995(5) SCC577 (SLAO Vs. Puttaiah and others), that the liability of the State to pay interest ceases with effect from the date of deposit.
.9. In order to prove their case, the claimant No. 2 Lakshmi K has been examined as PW.1 and GPA holder of claimant No. 4 has been examined as PW.2.

The documents marked at Ex.P.1 to 36.
.10.

On the basis of the above, the points for consideration is that:
"Whether the claimants 2 and 4 prove that they are the absolute owners of the acquired property and entitled for the compensation amount deposited to the Court?"
.11.

Heard the arguments, perused the materials on record, on that basis, my finding on the above point is in the affirmative for the following:
L.A.C. No. 133/2016 REASONS .12.
Point: This is a reference filed under Sections 30 and 31 of L.A. Act for apportionment of compensation as well as to decide the title of rival claimants regarding acquired property.

The claimants 2 and 4 have made out identical case, as such, it is for these claimants to prove their better title over the acquired property as well as entitlement for the compensation regarding acquired property.
.13.

The claimants 2 and 4 have filed separate claim statements that are identical to each other and they are claiming their share over the acquired land and claiming right over 3 Sq.
Meters each of acquired property.

.14. The definite case of the claimants 2 and 4 is that the acquired property originally belongs to one Smt. Geetha and others and they have sold L.A.C. No. 133/2016 the said property to Smt. Gopamma, Smt. Lakshmi and G.C. Chandrashekar, who are claimants 1 to 3 herein under a registered sale deed dated 27.11.1989.
Subsequently the claimants 1 to 3 partitioned their properties under the registered partition deed dated 22.03.1991.

sentences.text: After the partition, the respective claimants have taken their possession of respective properties allotted to their respective shares.

It is also claimed that the claimants 1 and 3 have no right over the acquired property as the property of claimant No.3 has not been acquired and claimant No.1 settled her right over the acquired property in favour of claimant No.4, who is her son.

In support of these contentions, the claimant No.2 examined herself as PW.1 and GPA holder of claimant No.4 examined as PW.2 by filing evidence affidavits wherein they have stated in-consonance L.A.C. No.
133/2016 with their respective claim statements.
Even the evidence affidavits of PW.1 and 2 are almost identical to each other.

PW.1 has produced RTC extracts of the property in Sy. No.33/2 at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.4, two encumbrance certificate at Ex.P.5 and 6, tax assessment of extract at Ex.P.7,
five tax paid challans at Ex.P.8 to 12, tax paid receipts at Ex.P.13 to 23, Aadhar card at Ex.P.24 and mutation extract at Ex.P.25.
Similarly, the GPA holder of claimant No.4 is examined as PW.2.
PW.2 has produced sale deed dated 25.10.1989 at Ex.P.27 and partition deed dated 22.03.1991 at Ex.P.28 along with khatha extracts in the names of claimants 1 and 4 at Ex.P.29 to Ex.P.34.
All these documents certainly substantiate the claim of claimants 2 and 4.

At this juncture, it is relevant to note that the memo filed by the claimant No.1 on 22.03.2018 reads as that:
L.A.C. No. 133/2016 " I submit that she do not have any right, interest over the property in question in the above case, the same has been transferred to Sri. D.V.
Gajendra who is the son of claimant No.1 and claimant No.4 herein through the registered family settlement dated 01.09.2017 and he is the absolute owner of the property in question.
Hence, he do not have any right, interest over the property in question, in the interest of justice."
The said memo has been signed by claimant No.1.
Therefore, as per the said memo, the claimant No.1 has given up her right over the acquired property under a registered family settlement dated 01.09.2017.
Of-course, the claimant No.1 or 4 have not produced the said settlement deed dated 01.09.2017 before the Court but that has been admitted by the parties to the case.
It is also relevant to note that there is no cross-examination of claimants 2 and 4 by each other.
Hence, it has to be inferred that claimants L.A.C. No. 133/2016 2 and 4 are claiming their right over 3 Sq. Meters each of the 6 Sq. Meters acquired property.
.15. As per the reference made to the Court, the LAO acquired 6 Sq. Meters of land in the property bearing Sy. No. 33/2 of Pattanagere village.

The evidence affidavits filed by PWs.1 and 2 at para No.6 disclose that total 6 Sq. Meters of property has been acquired and the claimants 2 and 4 are claiming 3 Sq. Meters each out of said 6 Sq. Meters of acquired property.
There is no dispute regarding acquisition of 6 Sq. Meters of acquired property and the claimants 2 and 4 are claiming 3 Sq. Meters each.
Hence, there is no dispute between the parties regarding extent of property claimed by them.
In the case on hand, the claimants 1 and 3 have not claimed right over the acquired property.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the parties discloses that 6 L.A.C. No.
133/2016 Sq. Meters of property has been acquired out of which, the claimants 2 and 4 are entitled for 3 Sq. Meters of land each, hence, the claimants 2 and 4 are entitled for compensation equally in respect of acquired property to an extent of 3 Sq. Meters each and claimants 1 and 3 are not entitled for any compensation.
Accordingly, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative.

1894 in respect of claimant No.2 Smt. Lakshmi K and claimant No.4 Gajendra is hereby allowed.
